title: One agent runtime and one tool registry
request: Extract one agent runtime: Tool, Registry, Policy and run(); register the 20 intern tools and the Home agent's tools once; make the MCP server list the registry. Do not change any tool's behaviour or name; keep the legacy names.
spec: dclab_rnd/agents/ with Tool (name, description, JSON schema, handler, read or write effect), Registry, Policy (system prompt, tool names, budget) and run(policy, state, gateway); run() asks the gateway, validates arguments against the schema (a bad call returns as an error the model can read), runs the tool, and loops until a final answer or the step or time budget. Done when adding a tool is one registration, the intern, the Home agent and /mcp all list it, and tests/test_mcp.py and tests/test_intern.py pass unchanged.
plan: Read the three tool sets: the intern's Toolbox, the Home agent's run_tool branches and the MCP server's list.
Write dclab_rnd/agents/ (registry.py, runtime.py) with scoped registries: 'project' for the intern and /mcp, 'draft' for the Home agent.

Move the intern's tools into the registry while keeping the Toolbox API (schemas, names, call) for the loop, MCP and tests; turn each Home run_tool branch into a registered handler; make /mcp read the list at each request.
Run the affected test files unchanged (94 passed), then write the package's own tests (a new tool appears in all three places).
Run check-all and the review; fix the four findings with tests; park the next package's work as a patch file (not git stash) so A2.1 is gated alone; commit.

decisions.decision: Keep the agents' own loops calling through Toolbox.call, which checks only unknown and missing arguments, until A2.4 moves them onto run().
decisions.why: The handlers clamp and coerce values (max_rows, k, industry); a full schema check in the old path would have changed behaviour, which the package forbids.

decisions.decision: An argument sent as null counts as not given, but an unknown argument stays unknown even when null.
decisions.why: Models in strict mode send null for every optional field; a null for a key the handler does not take would still crash it.

decisions.decision: Make jsonschema a declared requirement in base and CI rather than an optional import.
decisions.why: With a silent fallback the schema check turned off in CI, so the package's claim depended on the environment.

change: dclab_rnd/agents/ with Tool (schema, handler, effect, legacy aliases), a scoped Registry with check levels, Policy and run(); the 20 intern tools and 8 Home tools registered once in default_registry(); /mcp lists the registry per request; jsonschema added to requirements/base.txt and requirements/ci.txt; tests/test_agents_runtime.py.

findings.defect: The schema check in Toolbox.call changed tool behaviour, which the package forbids.
findings.scenario: Calls that worked before were refused: set_solution with time_column, group_column and metric set to null; get_results with stage null; set_settings with max_rows 100 (the handler clamped to 200) or '5000' (the handler converted it); create_project with industry 'retail' (the store fell back to 'general'); search_evidence with k 50.
findings.cause: The full JSON-schema check ran in the old call path, ahead of handlers that were written to be lenient.
findings.fix: Registry.check has levels: full schema in run(), names only (unknown and missing) in Toolbox.call until A2.4; a null counts as not given.
findings.test: test_a_null_counts_as_not_given and the unchanged intern and MCP tests.

findings.defect: CI would fail, and the schema check silently turned off without jsonschema.
findings.scenario: The CI workflow installs only requirements/ci.txt (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, pyarrow). Blocking the jsonschema import made three runtime tests error: two handlers raised TypeError instead of returning an error, and the registry well-formedness test failed with ImportError.
findings.cause: jsonschema came only transitively through the agent lock file, and the code had an ImportError fallback.
findings.fix: jsonschema>=4.18 in base and CI requirements; the fallback removed.
findings.test: The runtime tests run in CI.

findings.defect: run() overran its step and time budgets within one model reply.
findings.scenario: Policy with max_steps 2 and one reply holding five tool calls: all five ran (steps 5), then the run stopped for steps. The intern loop it replaces checked the budget before each call.
findings.cause: Budgets were checked only before asking the model.
findings.fix: The budget is checked before every call; a call past the budget gets a 'budget exhausted' tool message and is not run.
findings.test: A runtime test with five calls under a budget of two.

findings.defect: run() kept executing calls after a terminal tool, and a stray argument named 'turn' crashed the Home handlers.
findings.scenario: One reply [finish, add]: add still ran after finish. Separately, run_tool(draft, 'get_profile', {'turn': 1}) raised 'got multiple values for argument turn', because every Home handler takes the turn as its first parameter.
findings.cause: The loop did not stop at a terminal tool, and the handler context shared a name space with model arguments.
findings.fix: After a terminal tool, the remaining calls get 'not run: the run ended'; the Home handlers' context is positional-only.

outcome: Done: dclab_rnd/agents holds Tool, a scoped Registry, Policy and run(); 20 project tools and 8 Home tools are registered once and /mcp reads the list per request; tests/test_mcp.py and tests/test_intern.py pass unchanged. The gate passed with 414 tests on files and on PostgreSQL and the four flows; four review findings fixed.
lessons: A refactor that adds validation in an existing path changes behaviour: lenient handlers depend on receiving what a strict schema would refuse.
An optional import with a silent fallback makes a safety check depend on the environment; declare the dependency.
A budget checked once per model reply is not a budget; check it before every call.
